questions.prompt: Which description best distinguishes a source harmonic from a formant in the supplied source–filter figures?

options.text: A harmonic is one of the regularly spaced source components, while a formant is a tract resonance reflected in the broader envelope of component amplitudes.
options.feedback: The narrow lines represent source-frequency components. Formants shape groups of their heights, so a resonance can lie between two harmonic frequencies rather than being identical to one line.

options.text: A harmonic is a broad resonance of the tract, while a formant is a narrow source line associated with the vocal folds’ repeated vibration.
options.feedback: Vocal-fold repetition supplies harmonic components, while tract resonances are formants. This exchanges their roles.

options.text: A harmonic names a low-frequency spectral component, while a formant names a higher-frequency component, separating the terms by their position on the frequency axis.
options.feedback: Their distinction concerns source versus filter, not a low-versus-high frequency division.

options.text: A harmonic becomes a formant when it is the tallest line in the spectrum, making amplitude rank the criterion that distinguishes the two quantities.
options.feedback: A tall harmonic can be strengthened near a resonance, but amplitude rank does not redefine it as a formant.

questions.answer: The narrow lines represent source-frequency components. Formants shape groups of their heights, so a resonance can lie between two harmonic frequencies rather than being identical to one line.
rubric: Identify individual source-frequency components as harmonics.
Identify formants as resonances represented in the spectral envelope.

options.text: The spectrum plots amplitude across frequency, while the spectrogram places time horizontally, frequency vertically, and larger amplitude in darker marks.

options.text: The spectrum plots amplitude across frequency, while the spectrogram places frequency horizontally, amplitude vertically, and elapsed time in its darkness levels.

options.text: The spectrum is a short time slice, while the spectrogram averages the slices into one frequency–amplitude curve and removes their time ordering.

options.text: The illustrated /i/ has lower source F0 than /a/, using the lower first formant as the measure of the vocal-fold repetition rate.

options.text: The falling separation between the first two bands indicates falling F0, because those bands should be read as adjacent source harmonics rather than resonant regions.
options.feedback: The identified bands are formants. Their separation is not the adjacent-source-harmonic spacing.

options.text: The first two resonance regions move closer together, with dark bands tracking their changing frequencies rather than reporting increasing and decreasing probability.
